extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of Euclidean geometry (readers/students of Book VI / similar-figures theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of Euclid Book VI: definitions, theorems, constructions and corollaries concerning similar rectilineal figures, proportionality, centres of similitude, areas (duplicate ratio), and related constructions (inscribing/escribing parallelograms, extreme and mean ratio, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of two similar figures on a given line (direct and inverse similarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a given line AB there can be constructed two figures each similar to a given figure CDEFG, and having the given line AB homologous to any given side CD of the given figure. The first is said to be directly similar, and the second inversely similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the construction AB is homologous to CD; the figure may be turned about AB to produce the inverse similarity. (Observation: This is the construction explained in the text; see reference to Hamilton's terminology.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: multiplicity of similar polygons on a given line
rubrics_metrics.description: Twice as many polygons may be constructed on AB similar to a given polygon CDEFG as that figure has sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because AB can be made homologous to any side and for each side two orientations (direct/inverse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: placement yields parallel homologous sides
rubrics_metrics.description: If the constructed figure ABHIJ be applied to CDEFG so that A coincides with C and AB is placed along CD, then points H, I, J lie on CE, CF, CG respectively; and sides BH, HI, IJ are respectively parallel to DE, EF, FG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the relative positions and parallels when homologous sides are placed aligned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: dividing lines from a point in same ratio produces similar parallel figure
rubrics_metrics.description: If lines drawn from any point O in the plane of a figure to all its angular points be divided in the same ratio, the lines joining the points of division will form a new figure similar to, and having every side parallel to, the homologous side of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct proportional divisions of rays from a center O; join division points to obtain a similar figure with parallel homologous sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: duplicate ratio (as used here)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duplicate ratio of two lines is taken (here, for the alternate proof) to be the ratio of the squares described on these lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes pupils find Euclid's original notion difficult and uses this square-based definition for the duplicate ratio in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIX — Areas of similar triangles (duplicate ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar triangles (ABC, DEF) have their areas to one another in the duplicate ratio of their homologous sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs given: Euclid's original using a third proportional, and an alternative using squares on homologous sides (see prior definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XX(1) — Division of similar polygons into similar triangles
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar polygons may be divided into the same number of similar triangles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide each polygon by joining a vertex to other vertices (or analogous diagonals); since polygons are equiangular and sides about equal angles are proportional, the corresponding triangles are equiangular and so similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XX(2) — Corresponding triangles preserve polygon ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding triangles (from the divisions in (1)) have the same ratio to one another which the polygons have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each triangle pair is in the duplicate ratio of the homologous sides; sums of antecedents and consequents preserve the same ratio as the polygons.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XX(3) — Similar polygons area ratio (duplicate ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar polygons are to each other in the duplicate ratio of their homologous sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from the triangle case: polygons decomposed into corresponding triangles, each pair in duplicate ratio -> whole polygons in duplicate ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: perimeters of similar polygons
rubrics_metrics.description: The perimeters of similar polygons are to one another in the ratio of their homologous sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perimeters sum corresponding homologous sides so ratio equals ratio of any pair of homologous sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: duplicate ratio equals ratio of squares on lines
rubrics_metrics.description: As squares are similar polygons, the duplicate ratio of two lines is equal to the ratio of the squares described on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit reminder to compare with the annotation/definition referenced earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: similar portions preserve ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar portions of similar figures bear the same ratio to each other as the wholes of the figures; similar portions of perimeters are to each other in the ratio of the whole perimeters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you take corresponding parts (portions) of similar figures or perimeters, they maintain the same ratios as the entire figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEF. i — Homologous points
rubrics_metrics.description: Homologous points in the planes of two similar figures are such that lines drawn from them to the angular points of the two figures are proportional to the homologous sides of the two figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the definition and shows how to construct corresponding points: construct triangle on corresponding base similar to a given triangle to find the homologous point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property: correspondence for every point (under DEF. i)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two figures are similar, to each point in the plane of one there will be a corresponding point in the plane of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct by joining a point to two vertices and constructing on the homologous base a similar triangle; the apex is corresponding point.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEF. ii — Centre of similitude (double point)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two figures be directly similar and in the same plane, there is a special point which, regarded as belonging to either figure, is its own homologous point with respect to the other; this is called the centre of similitude or double point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: take two homologous sides AB, A'B' and describe circles on triads A,A',C and B,B',C whose second intersection gives O, the centre of similitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property: regular polygons and centers of similitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Two regular polygons of n sides each have n centres of similitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated without proof as a consequence of symmetry and the preceding definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property: common centre for many similar triangles on three lines
rubrics_metrics.description: If any number of similar triangles have their corresponding vertices lying on three given lines, they have a common centre of similitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric concurrency property derived from similarity constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property: parallel homologous sides imply all pairs parallel
rubrics_metrics.description: If two figures be directly similar, and have a pair of homologous sides parallel, every pair of homologous sides will be parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to define homothetic figures (next definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: DEF. iii — Homothetic figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Two figures are said to be homothetic if they are directly similar and have a pair of homologous sides parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, one is a dilation+translation/rotation of the other with centre of similitude as concurrency of corresponding lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property: concurrency to centre of similitude for homothetic figures
rubrics_metrics.description: If two figures be homothetic, the lines joining corresponding angular points are concurrent, and the point of concurrence is the centre of similitude of the figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard homothety property: corresponding vertices connected meet at a single centre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property: turning around centre produces homothety
rubrics_metrics.description: If two polygons be directly similar, either may be turned about their centre of similitude until they become homothetic, and this may be done in two different ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotation about the centre of similitude aligns sides to give parallel homologous sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: circles and sectors as similar figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Two circles are similar figures; sectors of circles having equal central angles are similar figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by dividing circles into many small (indefinitely small) triangles to make correspondence. Sectors with equal central angles are similar by direct construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property: infinite centres of similitude for circles; locus
rubrics_metrics.description: Two circles have an infinite number of centres of similitude; their locus is the circle whose diameter is the line joining the two points for which the two circles are homothetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because any two corresponding points can be chosen on the circles, giving a continuum of centres; the locus description given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: areas of circles proportional to squares of diameters
rubrics_metrics.description: The areas of circles are to one another as the squares of their diameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide each circle into equal similar elementary triangles: areas of these triangles are in duplicate ratio of radii/diameters; summing gives overall square proportionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: circumferences proportional to diameters
rubrics_metrics.description: The circumferences of circles are as their diameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from similarity of circles and proportionality of corresponding linear measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: circumference and arc proportional relations for equal central angles
rubrics_metrics.description: The circumference (and arcs) of sectors having equal central angles are proportional to their radii; for arcs a, a' and radii r, r', a : a' = r : r'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from similar elementary triangle decomposition or proportionality of central angles and radii.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula: area of a circle (and sector) via arc and radius
rubrics_metrics.description: The area of a circle is equal to half the rectangle contained by the circumference and the radius; the area of a sector of a circle is equal to half the rectangle contained by the arc of the sector and the radius of the circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argued by dividing circle into elementary triangles and summing: area = 1/2 * circumference * radius; sector area = 1/2 * arc * radius.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXI — Transitivity of similarity for rectilineal figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectilineal figures (A, B) which are similar to the same figure (C) are similar to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because both A and B are equiangular to C and have sides about equal angles proportional to C, hence A and B are equiangular and corresponding sides proportional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: homothetic transitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Two similar rectilineal figures which are homothetic to a third are homothetic to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct application of transitivity: if both homothetic to same figure, they share centre relations and homothety.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXII — Proportionality of figures described on proportional lines
rubrics_metrics.description: If four lines (AB, CD, EF, GH) be proportional, and any pair of similar rectilineal figures be similarly described on the first and second, and any pair on the third and fourth, these figures are proportional. Conversely, if figures described on first and second are to each other as figures on third and fourth, the four lines are proportional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses that figure area described on a line is as square of that line (ABK : CDL :: AB^2 : CD^2). Notes correction in some texts: figures should be similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXIII — Equiangular parallelograms and rectangle products
rubrics_metrics.description: Equiangular parallelograms (AD, CG) are to each other as the rectangles contained by their sides about a pair of equal angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sides about equal angles are AB, BC and BD, BG then parallelogram areas are proportional to AB·BD : BC·BG (compound ratio of two side ratios).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXIV — Parallelograms about a diagonal are mutually similar
rubrics_metrics.description: In any parallelogram, every two parallelograms which are about a diagonal are similar to the whole and to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because they share an angle and sides about equal angles are proportional (parallel sides give proportional triangles), so parallelograms AF, FC, AC are pairwise similar and homothetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXV — Construction: describe rectilineal figure equal to a given one and similar to another
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a figure A and another figure BCD (to be the similarity model), construct on side BC a rectangle BE equal to BCD, on CE describe EF equal to A, find mean proportional GH between BC and CF, and on GH describe figure GHI similar to BCD so that BC and GH are homologous sides; then GHI is equal to A and similar to BCD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative method: describe squares equal to BCD and A, find a fourth proportional and describe the similar figure on it. This is a constructive algorithm for producing a figure both equal in area to one figure and similar to another.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXVI — Similarly situated parallelograms with common angle share diagonal
rubrics_metrics.description: If two similar and similarly situated parallelograms have a common angle, they are about the same diagonal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide into similar triangles; a triangle FAG similar to CAD implies F lies on AC, so diagonals coincide.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXVII — Inscribe maximum parallelogram with common angle in triangle
rubrics_metrics.description: To inscribe in a given triangle ABC the maximum parallelogram having angle B in common with the triangle: bisect the opposite side AC at P and draw through P parallels to the other sides; BP is the maximum parallelogram required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof compares any other inscribed parallelogram BD and shows BP has larger area; corollaries: relationship of differences between parallelograms and proportionality of inscribed parallelograms to rectangles of partitioned sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXVIII — Inscribe parallelogram equal to given figure not exceeding maximum
rubrics_metrics.description: Given triangle ABC and a rectilineal figure X not greater than the maximum inscribed parallelogram, there is a construction (bisect AC at P, draw PF, PE, produce EP, draw CJ, construct parallelogram KLMN equal to the difference between PJCF and X and similar to PJCF, cut off PI equal to KL, draw IH parallel to AB cutting AC at D, draw DG parallel to BC) so that BD is the required parallelogram equal to X and having angle B common with triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive procedure using differences of similar parallelograms; relies on similarity about diagonals and equality/difference relations established earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXIX — Escribe parallelogram equal to given figure with common external angle
rubrics_metrics.description: To escribe (construct exterior to) a given triangle ABC a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure X and having an angle common with an external angle B: similar construction as Prop. XXVIII but making K N equal to the sum (excess) rather than the difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous constructive method; proof parallels that of the previous proposition using sums/differences of parallelograms.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXX — Divide a line in extreme and mean ratio (golden section construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: To divide a given line AB in extreme and mean ratio: divide AB in C so that the rectangle AB·BC equals the square on AC; then C is the point required (i.e., AB : AC :: AC : CB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructively find C so AB·BC = AC^2; proofs use proportion manipulations to show AC is mean proportional and the division is the extreme and mean ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXI — Generalized Pythagoras for similar figures on triangle sides
rubrics_metrics.description: If any similar rectilineal figure be similarly described on the three sides of a right-angled triangle ABC, the figure on the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of those described on the two other sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: relate figures by duplicate ratios to sides and use a^2 + b^2 = c^2; alternate proof uses proportional notation α : γ :: a^2 : c^2 etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXII — Collinearity from proportional sides and contained angle
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles (ABC, CDE) have two sides of one proportional to two sides of the other (AB : BC :: CD : DE) and the contained angles (B, D) equal, and are joined so homologous sides are parallel, then the remaining sides are in the same right line (collinear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equiangularity and angle sums to show the relevant lines form supplementary/right-angle relations, leading to collinearity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXIII — In equal circles: ratios of arcs, angles, and sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: In equal circles, angles at the centres or at the circumferences have the same ratio to one another as the arcs on which they stand, and so also have the sectors. Thus BC : EF :: angle BOC : EPF :: sector BOC : sector EPF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: take equimultiples of arcs/angles to compare using equimultiplicity principle; for sectors relate sector area to arc × radius (and note earlier formula for circle area).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: centre of mean position of a system of points
rubrics_metrics.description: The centre of mean position of any number of points A,B,C,D,... is found by iterated bisection/division: bisect AB at G, join G to C and divide GC so GH = GC, join H to D and divide HD so HK = HD, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure defines an iterative geometric mean-position (centroid-like) construction for an arbitrary number of points.
